lesson.title: Moving Points Across the Plane
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 2, Session 5
lesson.fileName: Session 5 - Moving Points Across the Plane.pptx

plan.curriculum: Mathematics 2.0, Space, Year 6 (VC2M6SP02): describe changes to the coordinates when a point is moved to a different position in the plane
plan.shape: short-cycle loops: model a move, try one, then a harder one, because crossing zero needs several small steps
plan.criticalFeature: moving left past zero keeps subtracting: 2 left of 1 is -1
decisionPoints: the hinge: move A 4 left and 2 down
plan.anchor: across the corridor, then up the stairs: (x, y), and the numbers sit on the lines
plan.catchUp: Missed Session 4? Show the sign chart (minus first is left, minus second is down) and read one point in each quadrant before the launch.

studentTools: A ruler and a sharp pencil for every student
Printed Worksheet for every student; Extension and Supported Worksheet as needed
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
boardSetup: The anchor on the board: across the corridor, then up the stairs, (x, y)
A number line from -5 to 5 under the four-quadrant grid, for counting across zero

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn. A table of moves across zero, translating a rectangle, describing translations, a mistake to fix and a treasure map.
resources.title: Moving Points Across the Plane
resources.subtitle: Left and right change the first number, up and down the second, even past zero.

example.prompt: (1, 2) moves 4 left. Where does it land?

items.prompt: Translate the rectangle 5 left and 3 down. Draw it and write its new corners.
What happened to the first number of every corner? What happened to the second number?
items.answer: Every first number went down by 5, and every second number went down by 3.

items.prompt: Ben moved (-2, 3) 4 right. Find his mistake and fix it.
items.answer: Right means add: -2 + 4 = 2, so the point is (2, 3).

example.prompt: The ship is at the origin. A crab at (2, -1) walks 3 left. Where is it?

items.prompt: Use coordinates to solve the treasure clues.

parts.prompt: The parrot at (3, 2) flies 7 left, 4 down. Where?

items.prompt: A point moves 3 left, then 3 right, then 2 up, then 2 down. Where does it end?
items.explain: The left and right moves cancel, and so do the up and down moves, so it ends where it started.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option. Finding a hidden translation, translation rules and your own puzzle, with worked examples.
resources.title: Extension: Translation Puzzles
resources.subtitle: Find the move, then use it.

example.prompt: A corner moved from (2, -1) to (-3, 2). Where did the corner (4, 1) go?

items.prompt: A shape moved so that (1, 1) landed on (-2, 4). Where did (3, -2) land?
A shape moved so that (-4, 2) landed on (1, -3). Where did (0, 0) land?

example.prompt: Rule: 2 left, 3 up. Where does (1, -1) go?

items.prompt: Use the rule 4 left, 2 down. Fill the gaps.

steps: Draw a triangle in one quadrant.
Choose a move that takes it into another quadrant.
Give a partner the start corners and the move.

items.prompt: Make a translation puzzle that moves a shape from the first quadrant into the third. Write the answer on the back.
items.answer: Check: the move is left and down, big enough that every corner ends with both numbers negative.

resources.label: Supported Worksheet
resources.description: For students who need more guidance: number-line jumps first, then arrows drawn on the grid, with a hint on every question.
resources.title: Moving Across Zero: Step by Step
resources.subtitle: Count the jumps on the number line.

items.prompt: Start at 3. Jump 4 left. Where do you land?
Start at -2. Jump 6 right. Where do you land?

slides.notes: Session 5 of our coordinates week: today we move points and shapes across zero, into other quadrants.
Before you start, put boards, markers, a ruler and a pencil on every desk. Print the Worksheet for everyone, and a few copies of the Extension and the Supported Worksheet.

beats: SAY: Let's warm up with fractions from last term.
ASK: What is three quarters plus one eighth?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 7/8
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> turn quarters into eighths on the fraction strips together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: Three quarters is six eighths, and one more eighth makes seven eighths.
Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 4/12.
Fix: show that you can only add parts of the same size,
and they rename the quarters as eighths.
notes.prep: Review of Term 3 fractions (the request named the focus). Keep the review under 6 minutes.

beats: ASK: What is two thirds of 18?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 12
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal and move straight on.
Less -> share 18 into 3 equal groups, then take 2 groups. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: One third of 18 is 6,
so two thirds is 12. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 6 or 9.
Fix: find one third first, then double it, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Term 3 review: a fraction of an amount.

beats: ASK: What is one half take away one fifth?
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 3/10
SCAN boards, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then on to Fluency.
Less -> rename both as tenths together on the board. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: One half is five tenths and one fifth is two tenths,
so the answer is three tenths. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 0/3 or 1/3.
Fix: rename both as tenths, five tenths and two tenths, and they redo it.
notes.prep: Term 3 review: subtracting fractions with different denominators.

beats: SAY: Now for our four times table.
This one's bigger, so double and double again.
ASK: What is 4 times 13?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 52
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> double 13, then double again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 52. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 42.
Fix: double 13 to get 26, double again to get 52, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Times tables fluency. Keep the whole block under 5 minutes.

beats: SAY: Now a division. How many fours make 36?
ASK: What is 36 divided by 4?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 9
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the next one.
Less -> halve 36, then halve again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 9. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 8.
Fix: check: 8 times 4 is 32,
one more four makes 36, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

beats: SAY: And a big one to finish.
ASK: What is 4 times 50?
8 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: 200
SCAN boards.
80%+ -> reveal, then the learning intention.
Less -> double 50, then double again. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's 200. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing 20 or 250.
Fix: double 50 to get 100, double again to get 200, and they rewrite it.
notes.prep: Brisk: one line of feedback, then the next.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to move points and shapes across the Cartesian plane and describe how their coordinates change.
successCriteria: I can move a point left, right, up or down in four quadrants.
I can write the new coordinates after a move, even when it crosses zero.
I can describe a translation using the change in each number.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: This week we've read, plotted and moved points.
Today we move them across zero, into other quadrants.
SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we start,
and the second one is our big goal today.
notes.prep: SC1 moving a point is reachable for everyone; SC2 writing the new coordinates across zero is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 describing a translation is the stretch.

slides.title: Jump across zero
slides.prompt: Start at 2. Jump 5 to the left. Where do you land?

beats: POINT to 2 on the number line.
SAY: Let's start on 2 and jump 5 to the left,
one jump at a time.
ASK: Where do you land after 5 jumps to the left?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: -3
SCAN boards for -3.
80%+ -> say: moving left on a grid works exactly like this.
Less -> jump together, counting 1, 0, -1, -2, -3. Re-ask.
SAY: We land on negative 3. Two jumps took us to zero,
and three more took us past it.
Points on a grid cross zero the same way.
trap: landing on -2 by counting 2 as a jump.
Fix: jump from 2, counting each jump, not each number, and they try again.
notes.prep: The launch comes after the LI: crossing zero on one number line before the grid. Under 4 minutes.

slides.meaning: The point (0, 0), where the two axes cross.
slides.example: Every point is measured from the origin.

beats: POINT to the word.
SAY: This word is origin. Say it with me: or-i-gin.
SAY: The origin is the point zero, zero, where the axes cross.
When a point crosses an axis, it passes through zero.
ASK: What are the coordinates of the origin?
5 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (0, 0)
trap: writing (1, 1).
Fix: trace both axes to where they cross, and they rewrite it.

slides.title: Crossing zero
steps: Move 5 left: left changes the first number.
2 - 5: back 2 to zero, then 3 more is -3.

beats: MODEL moving P five squares left.
SAY: Let me move P five squares to the left, counting as I go.
POINT to the axis as P crosses it.
SAY: Two squares take me to zero, and three more take me past it.
So the first number goes from 2 down to negative 3.
ASK: The second number didn't change. So what are P's new coordinates?
10 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (-3, 1)
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It's negative 3, 1. Moving left kept subtracting,
even after we passed zero.
trap: writing (3, 1).
Fix: count the jumps along the number line, and they add the sign.
notes.stretch: What move would take P back to where it started?
notes.help: Use the number line under the grid to count the jumps.
notes.prep: The critical feature: left keeps subtracting past zero. SC2.

slides.title: Translate a shape
steps: Move every corner the same way.
3 left: take 3 from each first number.
4 down: take 4 from each second number.

beats: POINT to the triangle.
SAY: Now I'll translate this triangle 3 left and 4 down.
Every corner moves the same way.
MODEL the corner (1, 1).
SAY: 1 take away 3 is negative 2,
and 1 take away 4 is negative 3.
So this corner lands on negative 2, negative 3.
ASK: Where does the corner 3, 1 land?
15 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (0, -3)
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: 3 take away 3 is 0, and 1 take away 4 is negative 3.
So it lands on 0, negative 3, right on the line going up.
trap: moving only one corner.
Fix: tick each corner as they move it, and they finish the shape.
notes.help: Make a table: old corner, new corner.
notes.prep: A translation is the same move for every corner. SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Where does it land?
slides.prompt: (1, -2) moves 3 left. Point to A, B or C

options.misconception: moves right instead of left: adds instead of subtracting
changes the second number for a left move

beats: SAY: Think about which number changes, and which way, before you choose.
ASK: If the point 1, negative 2 moves 3 left, where does it land?
15 sec. Cue: Voices off. Point... now. Hold your point.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then cold call one student: Why isn't it C?
Less -> jump left from 1 on the number line together. Re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: It's B. 1 take away 3 is negative 2,
and the second number stays negative 2.
trap: pointing to A.
Fix: jump left on the number line together, and they choose again.
notes.prep: First decision point. A means left was added; C means the wrong number moved.

slides.title: Where does it land?
slides.pivot: count the jumps on the number line together
slides.followUp: cold call one board: Which number changed, and how?

items.text: (-3, 1) moved to (2, -2). What was the move?
items.say: It moved 5 right and 3 down. Compare each number.

say: Write where each point lands on your board.
trap: forgetting the minus sign after crossing zero.
Fix: count the jumps past zero, and they add the sign.
notes.stretch: Name the quadrant the point starts in and ends in.
notes.help: Sketch a number line on your board and jump along it.
notes.prep: Guided practice crossing zero each way, then two moves, then a reverse question. SC2 and SC3.

beats: SAY: This one is just for you.
Move A 4 left and 2 down.
ASK: Where does A land?
20 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (-3, -1)
SCAN every board, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, then Your turn.
Less -> move A one square at a time on the big grid. Re-ask.
REVEAL after boards are scanned.
SAY: It lands on negative 3, negative 1.
1 take away 4, and 1 take away 2. Tick it or fix it.
trap: writing (-3, 1).
Fix: count the down jumps past zero, and they fix the second number.
notes.prep: The hinge before independent work: both numbers cross zero. Anyone who wrote (5, 3) or (-3, 1) starts on the Supported Worksheet with the teacher.

slides.title: Your turn
slides.task: Move points and shapes across zero on your worksheet.

beats: POINT to the steps.
SAY: Read each question carefully, solve it carefully, then check your answers.
SAY: If you finish, the Extension is your early finisher option.
Let's read the steps together. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE and ask: Did your point cross zero? How do you know?
TIME: 20 minutes. Stop everyone once at 10 minutes to share a strategy.
trap: adding for a left move.
Fix: ask which way left goes on the number line, and they redo it.
notes.stretch: Extension: finding a hidden translation, translation rules and your own puzzle.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: number-line jumps, then arrows on the grid, with hints.
notes.prep: Independent practice: moves across zero, a translation, describing moves, a mistake and a treasure map. The sheet is evidence for SC2 and SC3.

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: N moves 5 right and 4 down. Write its new coordinates.

beats: SAY: Here's the last one. Work it out on your own board.
ASK: Where does N land after 5 right and 4 down?
25 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: (3, -1)
RECORD who misses a sign or changes the wrong number.
Their names go to next week's catch-up group.
trap: writing (3, 7) or (-7, -1).
Fix: none now. Record the name for tomorrow.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 across the week: both numbers change and one crosses zero.

slides.reflectionPrompt: Tell your partner how you move a point across zero.

notes.answer: open - listen for keep subtracting past zero and add the minus sign
beats: SAY: Let's read our I can statements together.
Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How sure are you that you can move points across the Cartesian plane?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit board.
A thumb up with a sign missing matters most.
ASK: How do you move a point across zero?
20 sec. Cue: Partner A first. You have 20 seconds. Go.
EXPECT: keep subtracting past zero and add the minus sign
notes.prep: Week close: read the self-assessment beside the exit evidence for next week's review.
